finding.claim: wipe() calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") but discards its boolean return value. requireRole only returns true or false and never throws, so the check has no effect. Any authenticated user can call repo.wipe(tenant) and destroy a tenant's data, whatever their roles. The sibling export() uses checkRole(), which throws, so the bug is specific to wipe().
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, with any role set (or none), and an attacker-chosen tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive wipe of tenant data.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe. Both u and tenant come from the request.
requireRole(u, "OWNER") is called as a bare statement. The result is ignored, so execution continues for non-owners.
requireRole is declared `static boolean` and returns u.roles().contains(role). The javadoc says "Does not throw", so a missing role produces no error.

finding.guards_checked: Searched the only source file, src/Admin.java. There is no other authorization layer, filter, or annotation on wipe(). checkRole (line 18) would throw on a missing role but is not used here. No try/catch or return-value check wraps the call. Whether a gateway or framework outside this repo enforces the role is unknown. Nothing in the repo does.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (Admin.java:14) returns boolean and never throws; its result is discarded at line 26. checkRole (line 18) throws but is only used in export() at line 32. No other guard, annotation, or try/catch exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:26 calls requireRole as a bare statement, discarding the boolean that Admin.java:14-15 returns without throwing, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any authenticated user.

finding.claim: The OWNER role check is global and not scoped to the tenant. Roles live in User.roles() with no tenant association, and the tenant argument is never compared with the user's membership. Even with AUTH-1 fixed, an OWNER of one tenant can export, or wipe, any other tenant by changing {t} in the URL. This is a cross-tenant IDOR. Confidence is lower than AUTH-1 because it depends on how roles are assigned outside this file.
finding.source: Authenticated user holding OWNER in their own tenant, supplying a different victim tenant ID in /tenants/{t}/export or /tenants/{t}/wipe.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33 (data exfiltration), and repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 (destruction).

trace.note: User record has only name and roles. No tenant binding.
export(User u, String tenant) takes tenant from the request path.
checkRole(u, "OWNER") tests only whether the string "OWNER" is in the set, regardless of tenant.
repo.export(tenant) runs against the attacker-chosen tenant.

finding.guards_checked: Looked for a tenant-membership check, a tenant-scoped role string, or ownership validation of `tenant` against `u`. None exists in the file. Repo implementations are not present, so a check inside Repo cannot be ruled out. Repo is only an interface here.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole(u,"OWNER") at Admin.java:32 (throws, but global, not tenant-scoped); requireRole at line 26 discards its result (wipe is unguarded). No tenant-membership check in the file or elsewhere in the repo.
verdict.reason: Admin.java:4 User has no tenant binding, and the only guard at :32 checks the role string alone before repo.export(tenant) at :33, so any OWNER can export any tenant; the wipe sink at :26-27 is also reachable, and is worse because requireRole's boolean is discarded. Repo is only an interface here, so an in-Repo check can't be ruled out, but nothing in the repo suggests one.
